summary:
Two different things are being felt at once, and they need to be separated before any code ships.

(1) The build under test multiplies everything. It is an EAS `development` profile dev client (Debug-compiled native: Fabric/Yoga/Reanimated/Worklets at -O0) running a Metro bundle with dev=true, minify=false: React's development build (an `Error()` stack capture for every JSX element created, prop validation), Hermes parsing source instead of loading bytecode, LogBox + console forwarding over Wi-Fi, the DevTools hook on every commit, lazy `import()` chunks fetched over Wi-Fi right after sign-in (RevenueCat, expo-notifications, expo-device), and the `__DEV__` reanimated `checkStyleOverwriting` builder run on every mount. None of that ships. It is the bulk of the general "everything is sluggish" feel, and it can be measured in ten minutes with `npx expo start --no-dev --minify`, and properly with `eas build --profile preview`.

(2) Underneath that there are real, code-verified, shipping costs, all of which come from the same root: `experiments.reactCompiler: true` is not compiling any hot component (37 bailouts, verified with the installed babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0). Three causes: `try { } finally { }` inside component bodies (Feed, CommentsScreen, FanMailScreen, ChatScreen, ShopScreen, ShowsScreen, media-pickers, ...), `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/*` anywhere in the component (PostCard, ChannelScreen, ComposeScreen, MiniPlayer, SeekBar, TabsLayout, providers), and `sharedValue.value = withTiming(...)` in press handlers (ScalePressable, TabButton, ReactionChip, UnlockPill). The feel passes were written as if auto-memoised (inline renderItem closures, inline `FadeOut.duration()` / `LinearTransition.duration()` builders, inline extraData arrays, inline context values) and none of it is. The concrete consequences the owner will still feel on a release build, in order:
- Typing in a comment thread: `draft` lives on the 1,062-line CommentsScreen, so every keystroke re-renders the whole screen and every mounted comment row (up to 40), and each row re-registers 3 native layout animations (row exiting, inner layout, cell itemLayoutAnimation) because the builders are new objects each render: ~120 worklet serialisations + JSI calls per character on the JS thread the controlled TextInput is waiting on.
- Tapping play/pause: expo-audio's `play()` is a synchronous native call that runs `AVAudioSession.setActive(true)` (50-300 ms mediaserverd IPC) on the JS thread, before the glyph-flip state commits; and because `keepAudioSessionActive` defaults to false, every play-after-pause pays it again.
- Tapping in a chat thread: any ChannelScreen state change (tap-for-time, realtime arrival, receipt, send) reconciles all ~50 mounted messages (~100 reanimated class components) because renderRun is an inline closure and extraData is a fresh array.
- Fan mail and compose: typed text is screen-root state on uncompiled screens, so every keystroke rebuilds the whole form (fan mail also rebuilds and pushes 4 layout-animation configs to native per keystroke).
- Always-on background load while music plays: three withTiming glides keep a 60-commits/s shadow-tree loop alive for the seek bar, mini-player hairline and voice-note line; the 2 Hz status context re-renders every mounted AudioPlayerCard + MiniPlayer; no `enableFreeze()`, so blurred tabs keep rendering.
- Smaller shipping costs: PostCard root carries an animated opacity on the same view as FadeIn/FadeOut (the repeated `[Reanimated] Property opacity` warning; dev-only log, but a real delete-time flash and 2 re-serialisations per card render); every optimistic write does an extra GET /auth/v1/user round trip before the insert; full-screen CALayer masks + a masked BlurView under every list; 0.97-alpha backgrounds with 18 pt shadows on the dock pill and the composer pill fall off Fabric's shadowPath fast path.

The plan below orders fixes by felt improvement per hour of work, marks each as shipping or dev-only, and gives exact edits with working-tree line numbers (verified today in C:/dev/s333xhub). Items 1-2 (play tap, comment typing) are the two the owner will notice most on a real build. Item 3 is fifteen minutes and turns the compiler back on for every press component. Do not use the dev client to judge whether any of this worked; use the preview build.
dev_only_share: Plainly: most of it. On the dev client every render storm listed here costs several times what it costs in release (dev React with a stack capture per JSX element, unminified source with no Hermes bytecode, Debug-compiled native, LogBox and console forwarding over Wi-Fi, the DevTools hook on every commit, and three lazy bundle fetches right after the tabs mount). My honest estimate is that well over half of the general "clicking and typing feels sluggish" impression will disappear on a preview/release build without a single code change, and the `--no-dev --minify` step in the test recommendation shows how much in ten minutes. What will NOT disappear, because it is real code cost that ships: (1) the play/pause tap stall (a blocking 50-300 ms native audio-session call on the tap path), (2) typing in a long comment thread (whole-screen re-render plus ~3 native layout-animation re-registrations per mounted row per keystroke), (3) tapping in a 50-message chat thread (full-thread reconcile), (4) whole-form re-render per keystroke on fan mail and compose (smaller, but real), and (5) the steady background load while a track plays. Those are ordered first below. The repeated Reanimated opacity warning and the RevenueCat "Error fetching offerings" line are dev-only noise (LogBox parse + Metro symbolicate per warning); they cost nothing in release, though the opacity conflict they point at is a genuine (small) shipping bug that fix 6 removes.
test_recommendation:
Do this before shipping any change on the basis of feel, and again after each batch.

STEP 1, ten minutes, no rebuild (measures the JS-side dev overhead): stop Metro; run `npx expo start --no-dev --minify` from C:/dev/s333xhub; on the iPhone force-quit the dev client and reopen the project from the launcher (do not press r/shake-reload; the reload path reuses the old bundle URL). Close the Chrome DevTools window if you ever pressed `j` in Metro (an attached frontend walks the fiber tree on every commit and puts Hermes in debugger mode); keep Performance Monitor and Element Inspector off. Two intentional differences are NOT bugs: the Shop tab shows the "coming soon" teaser because src/lib/shop.ts:18 gates it on `__DEV__ || EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOP_TAB_LIVE === 'true'` (add `EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOP_TAB_LIVE=true` to .env if you want it live), and the RevenueCat red toast disappears (LogBox does not exist in this mode). Caveat: this mode still runs the Debug native binary and source JS (no bytecode), so "crisp now" proves the dev costs were it, but "still sluggish" does not yet prove an app-side cost. Optional for the dev client itself: start Metro with `$env:EXPO_NO_METRO_LAZY='1'; npx expo start` (PowerShell) so the whole graph is in the initial bundle and the first seconds after sign-in stop stalling on RevenueCat/expo-notifications chunk fetches; it makes the first load slower and the session smoother.

STEP 2, the real answer: `eas build --profile preview --platform ios` (eas.json already has it: Release configuration, `__DEV__=false`, hermesc bytecode embedded, no Metro/LogBox/DevTools, same `distribution: internal` ad-hoc provisioning as the dev build so the registered iPhone works). Judge tap and typing feel ONLY on this build; keep the dev build for functional checks. If shop feel matters, add `"env": {"EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOP_TAB_LIVE": "true"}` to the preview profile rather than reading the teaser as a regression.

WHAT TO TEST on the preview build, before and after each fix, on a physical iPhone: (a) open a post with 40+ comments, focus the composer, type 20 characters fast, watch the send disc enable and the pill grow (fix 2); (b) on an audio post tap play, pause, play, pause five times and watch the glyph (fix 1); (c) in a 50-message chat, tap a bubble to show its time, then send a message (fix 9); (d) fan mail: pick a photo, type a note (fix 4); (e) compose: type a body while a poll is on (fix 5); (f) leave a track playing and repeat (a) and (c) (fixes 8, 10). For the GPU-only items (12, 13) use Xcode > Debug > View Debugging > Rendering > Color Offscreen-Rendered Yellow, or Instruments > Core Animation FPS while scrolling the feed and tapping a reaction chip. For the compiler items, after each change run the 30-line babel logger check (item 15) and confirm the named component reports CompileSuccess; in Metro, confirm the "skipped optimizing" lines for compose.tsx are gone. A tap on a chat bubble should re-render exactly one RunRow (console.count inside it), and a keystroke in comments should re-render only Composer.

fixes.title: Play/pause tap: move audio-session activation off the tap path and keep the session warm
fixes.felt_effect: The play glyph flips the instant you tap instead of after a 50-300 ms freeze, on the most-tapped control in a music app; play-after-pause stops paying the full activation again. Ships. About 20 minutes.

fixes.title: Comment thread typing: give the draft its own component and stop rebuilding layout-animation configs per row
fixes.felt_effect: Typing in comments stops lagging: a keystroke re-renders one 20-line component instead of the whole 1,062-line screen plus every mounted comment row with ~3 native layout-animation re-registrations each. Send-disc enable and pill growth follow the keyboard immediately. Biggest typing win in the app, and it scales with thread length. Ships. About 1-2 hours including the row memo.

fixes.title: Turn the React Compiler back on for every press component: sharedValue.value = x -> sharedValue.set(x)
fixes.felt_effect: ScalePressable, TabButton, ReactionChip and UnlockPill (every acknowledgment animation in the app) start compiling, so their inline handlers, style arrays and animated-style factories are memoised instead of rebuilt on every parent render. Small per tap, app-wide, and fifteen minutes. Ships.

fixes.title: Fan mail note: uncontrolled input, hoisted builders, and let the screen compile
fixes.felt_effect: Typing a fan-mail note no longer re-renders the whole tab (pitch card, pick/draft rows, three picker buttons, the SENT list with timeAgo per item) or pushes four layout-animation configs to native per keystroke. Ships. About 30 minutes.

fixes.title: Compose screen: delete the effect suppression and restructure handlePost so ComposeScreen compiles; hoist the upload-row builders
fixes.felt_effect: Typing a post body stops rebuilding the whole New Post form (ProjectPicker, poll box, thumbnail strip, audio box, three uncompiled picker buttons, the lock Switch and price chips) per keystroke: after the change only the body TextInput, canPost and handlePost recompute per character. Taps on the poll toggle, lock row and chips re-render far less. Ships. About 1 hour.

fixes.title: PostCard: one owner for opacity, hoisted builders, exiting only when deleting (kills the Reanimated warning and a real delete flash)
fixes.felt_effect: The '[Reanimated] Property opacity ... may be overwritten' warnings (four per feed render, each a LogBox parse + Metro symbolicate in dev) stop; deleting a post fades the dimmed card instead of snapping bright first; every PostCard re-render (reaction tap, poll vote, menu, any mediaUrls/social change) stops re-serialising two worklets and making a JSI call; recycled rows in long feeds unmount instantly instead of being held 180 ms off-screen. Small per tap, larger on feed-load bursts. Ships. About 30 minutes.
fixes.exact:
C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/post-card.tsx

1. Module scope (builders are immutable after construction; `.delay()` mutates, so the staggered ones are a precomputed array, never a shared constant chained further):
```ts
const CARD_EXIT = FadeOut.duration(180);
const CARD_LAYOUT = LinearTransition.duration(220); // matches the feed cell's 220 so surface and rows glide together
const CARD_ENTER = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((i) => FadeInDown.duration(280).delay(i * 50));
const ROW_ENTER = FadeInDown.duration(160);
const NOTICE_ENTER = FadeIn.duration(150);
const TAG_ENTER = FadeInDown.duration(220);
```
L576-577: `const rowEnter = reduceMotion ? undefined : ROW_ENTER; const noticeEnter = reduceMotion ? undefined : NOTICE_ENTER;`. L685-686: `TAG_ENTER`.

2. L580-592, split the root so the view carrying entering/exiting has no `opacity` in its style (exactly what the warning asks for):
```tsx
<Animated.View
  entering={animateIn && !reduceMotion ? CARD_ENTER[Math.min(index ?? 0, 4)] : undefined}
  exiting={deleting && !reduceMotion ? CARD_EXIT : undefined}
  style={styles.cardSlot}>
  <Animated.View
    layout={reduceMotion ? undefined : CARD_LAYOUT}
    style={[styles.card, post.project === 's333xgod' ? styles.cardGod : styles.cardMazze, dimStyle]}>
    ...existing children unchanged...
  </Animated.View>
</Animated.View>
```
(`deleting` is the existing state set at L546 before `deletePost` runs, so the exit config is registered before the row is removed; rows that VirtualizedList recycles during a scroll no longer fade off-screen.) If you would rather the card surface snap and only the feed cell glide, drop the inner `layout` prop entirely; do not remove `itemLayoutAnimation` in feed.tsx instead, handleDeleted's "list closes up" depends on it.

3. Styles L933-944: add `cardSlot: { marginHorizontal: 14, marginBottom: 14 },` and delete those two keys from `card` (background, radius, padding, border, shadow stay on `card`). Geometry is identical; the whole surface still dims to 0.5 on delete.

4. C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/feed.tsx: module scope `const ITEM_LAYOUT = LinearTransition.duration(220);` and L330 `itemLayoutAnimation={reduceMotion ? undefined : ITEM_LAYOUT}` so every cell wrapper stops reconfiguring LAYOUT on every Feed state change.

Verify: no opacity warning in Metro on feed mount; delete a post and confirm the fade; scroll a 40+ post feed and confirm no off-screen fades.

fixes.title: Drop the extra auth round trip in front of every optimistic write
fixes.felt_effect: Chat send, reaction, poll vote, purchase, fan mail and report reconcile after ONE network round trip instead of two (supabase.auth.getUser() always does a GET /auth/v1/user; the id is already in the local session). Feed reactions/polls first paint drops one serial auth hop. This is the 'did it go through' delay, not the first-frame tap acknowledgement. Ships. About 15 minutes.

fixes.title: Stop the 60-commits-per-second loop while music plays (seek bar, mini-player hairline, voice-note line)
fixes.felt_effect: While a track plays, the three withTiming glides currently keep a shadow-tree commit + Yoga layout + mount diff running every frame on the main thread (on iOS with reanimated 4.5.1's default flags every animated prop, transform and opacity included, goes through commitUpdates), and the feed's copy sits inside a MaskedView that re-composites on each one. Stepping to each 500 ms tick drops that to 2 commits/s; the sub-pixel sweep it replaces is invisible on anything longer than ~30 s. Every tap and keystroke made while audio plays gets the main thread back. Ships. About 15 minutes.

fixes.title: Chat thread: a memoised RunRow so a tap re-renders one row, not fifty messages
fixes.felt_effect: Tapping a bubble for its time, a realtime arrival, a receipt refresh, a media URL landing or an optimistic send stops reconciling ~100 reanimated class components (Animated.View + TimeLabel + AvatarLift per message, segmentBody regex per text) on the JS thread; the next tap no longer queues behind that render. Chat typing is already isolated in Composer and is unaffected either way. Ships. About 2-3 hours; the largest single edit in the plan, so it sits after the cheap wins.
fixes.exact:
C:/dev/s333xhub/src/app/channel/[id].tsx (working-tree lines)

1. Hoist the send/mic swap builders next to ENTER_MINE/ENTER_THEIRS (L170-175): `const SWAP_IN = FadeIn.duration(120); const SWAP_OUT = FadeOut.duration(120);` and use them at L439-440 and L449-450, so each keystroke in Composer no longer re-registers the exiting config on the swap.

2. Extract renderRun (L1260-1339) + renderMessage (L1138-1258) into a module-level `const RunRow = memo(function RunRow(props) { ... })` with only shallow-comparable, per-run props: `run`, `isArtist`, `reduceMotion`, `expandedKey` (computed in renderItem: `run.messages.some((m) => stableKey(m) === expandedId) ? expandedId : null`), `receiptId`/`receiptSeen` (null unless `receipt.id` is in this run), `mediaSig` (`run.messages.map((m) => (m.media_path ? mediaUrls[m.media_path] ?? '' : '')).join('|')`, so text-only runs never re-render on URL resolution), `freshKeys` (`run.messages.filter((m) => freshIds.current.has(stableKey(m))).map(stableKey).join(',')`, computed in renderItem so RunRow never reads a ref during render; entering is mount-only so a later change is harmless), and callbacks `onToggleTime(key)`, `onLongPress(m)`, `onRetry(m)`, `onOpenProfile(id)`, `onLinkError()`. No eslint suppressions and no `ref.current` in RunRow's render, so the compiler compiles it (it already compiles TimeLabel/AvatarLift/Composer in this file); `memo` is still required because the compiler does not skip the call on parent re-render.

3. Stable callbacks in ChannelScreen: setExpandedId/setActionTarget/setError are already stable; `showProfile` is already a useCallback (profile-card.tsx:70); retrySend (L856) is a plain inner function, so `const retrySendRef = useRef(retrySend); useEffect(() => { retrySendRef.current = retrySend; }); const onRetry = useCallback((m: Message) => retrySendRef.current(m), []);`.

4. Delete the `extraData` array at L1368 entirely (actionTarget/reporting are not read by rows; CellRenderer never sees extraData) and render `<RunRow ... />` from a plain renderItem. Do not rely on useCallback(renderRun) for the win: FlatList without strictMode re-wraps renderItem every render; the memo bailout on RunRow is what saves the work.

5. Keep run identity stable across setMessages: buildRuns (L132-164) allocates fresh Run objects, so a send's three setMessages would still re-render all ~25 rows. In the `runs` useMemo (L1095) keep the previous result in a ref keyed by run.key and reuse the previous Run object when `separator`, `mine`, `artist`, `messages.length` and every `messages[i]` reference are identical (message references already survive appendNew/runSend/loadOlder). O(n) pass.

6. Optional: pass `reduceMotion` down as a prop to TimeLabel/AvatarLift instead of each calling useReduceMotion (one TurboModule call + listener per instance, ~100 per page at mount).

Sanity check: console.count inside RunRow; a bubble tap logs once, a send logs one or two.

fixes.title: Stop background work while you tap and type: enableFreeze, status only for the current audio card, compiled MiniPlayer
fixes.felt_effect: Blurred sibling tabs stop rendering on every context update (enableFreeze); the 2 Hz player-status tick stops re-rendering every mounted AudioPlayerCard in every mounted feed window (only the current track's card subscribes); MiniPlayer stops rebuilding its whole tree, a fresh expo-image source object and an entering builder twice a second. Only matters while a track plays or a tab is in the background, so secondary, but it is the steady load under everything else. Ships. About 1 hour.
fixes.exact:

Scope to state honestly: blurred sibling tabs inside (tabs) freeze; the screen directly under a pushed route (channel/[id], post/[id], compose) and iOS modals never freeze, so this alone does not speed up chat typing. Verify afterwards that the chat tab still reloads on return (useFocusEffect at chat.tsx:143) and feed scroll position survives a tab round-trip.

2. C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/audio-player-card.tsx L305-359: keep `usePlayerControls()` in AudioPlayerCard and move the `usePlayerStatus()` read (L307) plus everything derived from it (isPlaying/duration/position/spinner, L311-316, and the JSX at L345-357) into two children rendered by `isCurrent`: `<LiveControls postId title ... />` that calls usePlayerStatus, and `<IdleControls onPress={handlePress} />` that renders the play glyph and `<SeekBar isCurrent={false} duration={0} position={0} seekTo={seekTo} />` without subscribing. Non-current cards then never re-render on the 500 ms tick. (A single subscriber, MiniPlayer, does not need this.)

3. C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/mini-player.tsx: remove the two `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` at L36 and L48 (after item 3's `.set()` change) so MiniPlayer compiles (verified: compiles once both are gone); for the reset-on-track-change effect either list `[current?.postId]` honestly or wrap the body in React 19.2's `useEffectEvent`; hoist `source={{ uri: current.artworkUrl }}` (L75) into a useMemo on `current.artworkUrl` if the compiler output shows it uncached.

Optional and larger, only if a profiler still shows the status tick: replace `useAudioPlayerStatus(player)` (player-provider.tsx L82) with `useEventListener(player, 'playbackStatusUpdate', onStatus)` from 'expo', write currentTime/duration/playing into shared values, setState only on transitions, and expose a `usePlayerStatusFor(postId)` built on useSyncExternalStore whose snapshot changes at most 1 Hz for the current post and never for others. Keep updateInterval at 500.

Also: C:/dev/s333xhub/src/app/(tabs)/shop.tsx L35 / src/lib/countdown.ts: render the countdown from a leaf `<Countdown to={drop.drops_at} />` that owns useNow() so the 1 s tick re-renders one Text instead of ShopScreen (dev-only until EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOP_TAB_LIVE ships).

fixes.title: Comments keyboard: native inset instead of an animated footer height
fixes.felt_effect: While the keyboard opens/closes on the comments screen (~0.3-0.5 s, the moment you tap the field), reanimated's 120 fps keyboard display link currently commits a new shadow tree + Yoga layout of the 40-row list every frame and fires onContentSizeChange/onLayout into VirtualizedList per frame. Replaced by UIKit's own keyboard curve: zero per-frame commits. Not a per-keystroke cost; a tap-into-field cost. Ships. About 15 minutes.

C:/dev/s333xhub/src/app/post/[id].tsx: delete `keyboardSpacer` (L168-171) and the footer `<Animated.View style={keyboardSpacer} />` (L759; keep the loadingMore skeleton and the fragment); add `automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets` to the `Animated.FlatList` at L695. Keep `composerLift` (translateY, L162-167) and the `contentContainerStyle` paddingBottom `insets.bottom + 130` (content padding adds to the native inset). Do NOT apply the equivalent rework to the chat composer (channel/[id].tsx L551-560 composerPad paddingBottom): it would be a behaviour rework of the core screen (inverted list + maintainVisibleContentPosition targets) for a cost bounded to the keyboard transition and ~10 Yoga nodes; re-profile after the comments change first.

fixes.title: Opaque fills on the three shadowed pills so Core Animation stops re-rasterising an 18 pt shadow every frame
fixes.felt_effect: The dock pill, the shop circle and the comments composer pill use rgba(...,0.97) backgrounds with shadowRadius 18; Fabric only sets layer.shadowPath for alpha > 0.999, so every tab-press animation frame, every keystroke, caret blink, keyboard slide and feed-scroll frame under the dock re-rasterises the shadow offscreen. GPU/render-thread cost, always-on while the dock or composer is visible; not JS latency. 0.97 was never a visible translucency. Ships. Three lines.
fixes.exact:
C:/dev/s333xhub/src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx L225 (`pill`) and L249 (`circle`): `backgroundColor: 'rgba(21, 24, 29, 0.97)'` -> `backgroundColor: '#15181d'`.
C:/dev/s333xhub/src/app/post/[id].tsx L1081 (`pill`, the composer): same change. Leave `flash` at L861 alone (same alpha, no shadow, no cost). fixes.title: Edge glass: drop the masked bottom BlurView and make the list mask switchable for an on-device A/B
fixes.felt_effect: Every list is wrapped in a full-screen CALayer mask (offscreen render of cards, shadows, images on every scroll frame and every in-list animation), and every root screen stacks a masked BlurView (a paused UIViewPropertyAnimator sampling the backdrop per frame) on top, under a scrim that already darkens the same band to 0.92 alpha. Shows up as the press animation itself stuttering inside lists, not as late onPressIn. Scroll/animation smoothness item, below the JS-thread causes. Ships. About 15 minutes.
fixes.exact: C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/edge-fade.tsx: (1) L104-113 delete the bottom `MaskedView` + `BlurView` block, keeping the SCRIM_REVERSED gradient at L122-129; this finishes what commit 0c40ec4 did for the top edge and makes the native branch match the web branch. Do not replace it with an unmasked BlurView strip (its inner edge shows as a hard line over the photo background). (2) L40-66 FadeMask: add a module constant `const LIST_MASK = true;` and return the plain `<View style={[styles.flex, style]}>{children}</View>` branch (L47) when it is false, so the owner can flip it and compare on the device; the visual difference is confined to the 68/90 pt bands where the scrim already sits at 0.52-0.92 alpha. If the dissolve is kept, keep exactly one MaskedView per screen and never nest another mask or blur inside it. (3) Verify with Instruments > Core Animation, 'Color Offscreen-Rendered Yellow' + FPS while scrolling the feed and tapping a ReactionChip: the full-screen yellow tint disappears, frame time drops ~1-3 ms. If LIST_MASK settles on false, @react-native-masked-view/masked-view and expo-blur become unused and can be removed later.

fixes.title: Feed refresh: fewer full passes over the mounted cards
fixes.felt_effect: A feed refresh (tab focus after 120 s, pull-to-refresh, new-post stale mark, each pagination batch) currently commits 3-4 separate state passes that each re-render every mounted PostCard, and per-card prop-sync effects double it, right when the fan starts scrolling/tapping. Cuts the card-touching commits and stops a no-op mediaUrls update from re-rendering the whole list. Ships. About 30-60 minutes.
fixes.exact:
C:/dev/s333xhub/src/components/feed.tsx
1. L96 short-circuit identical URL maps: `setMediaUrls((prev) => { for (const k in urls) if (prev[k] !== urls[k]) return { ...prev, ...urls }; return prev; });`
2. L110 move `setPurchasedIds(purchased);` down to sit immediately before `setPosts(fresh);` (L116) so React batches them (resolveMedia already uses the local `purchased`; purchasedRef is only read on later user actions).
3. L328 hoist `keyExtractor` to a module function `const keyExtractor = (item: Post) => item.id;` and put the RefreshControl `onRefresh` (L333-) in a useCallback.
4. Module scope `const FOOTER_IN = FadeIn.duration(180);` for L352/L357/L378 (entering, so allocation-only; optional).

Optional, larger: have resolveMedia return the url map instead of setting it so loadFresh can commit mediaUrls in the same synchronous block as setSocial/setPolls/setTopFans (touches four call sites); and in post-card.tsx replace the two mirror effects at L455-462 with the render-phase 'adjust state when a prop changes' pattern (store prevReactions/prevPoll in state; when `reactions !== prevReactions` call the setters during render) so a props change is one committed render, not two. Keep the resync-on-identity-change semantics.
6. Do not use unstable_batchedUpdates (React 19 already batches per macrotask; it cannot merge across network responses).

fixes.title: Regression gate: fail lint on the three compiler-bailout patterns and add a compiler scan script
fixes.felt_effect: No feel change by itself; it stops the next feel pass from silently re-introducing try/finally, react-hooks suppressions or `.value =` handler writes and turning the compiler off again. No new dependency: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 and babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 are already installed via eslint-config-expo / babel-preset-expo. Tooling. About 30 minutes.

fixes.title: DEV ONLY: filter RevenueCat's native log stream at the source instead of after LogBox has parsed it
fixes.felt_effect: The recurring 'Error fetching offerings' (and every other SDK log line) currently crosses the bridge as console.* on each launch, is serialised to Metro over Wi-Fi and goes through LogBox's parse pipeline; the ignoreLogs regex only hides the toast afterwards. fixes.exact: From C:/dev/s333xhub: (a) `npx expo start --no-dev --minify` for a production-mode JS bundle in the existing dev client; force-quit and reopen from the launcher, do not shake-reload. (b) `$env:EXPO_NO_METRO_LAZY='1'; npx expo start` (PowerShell) to put the whole graph in the initial bundle so the three `await import()` calls fired by (tabs)/_layout.tsx L179-193 (configurePayments -> react-native-purchases, registerPushToken -> expo-device + expo-notifications, installPushNavigation -> expo-notifications) stop stalling the first seconds after sign-in; the variable is read by the CLI on the laptop. (c) Close the Chrome DevTools window if `j` was ever pressed in Metro; keep Performance Monitor and Element Inspector off. (d) Expect the Shop tab teaser (shop.ts:18 `__DEV__` gate) and no RevenueCat toast in --no-dev mode; neither is a bug. Do NOT convert the lazy `import()` calls to static imports to 'fix' (b): it gains nothing in production and drops the deliberate graceful degradation each one exists for. The honest benchmark remains `eas build --profile preview --platform ios`.
